observationsNotFindings: This is a document class I have not reviewed before in this chain — a booked laterAct discharging a source-search limb rather than a join, catalog, corpus or harness. Its correctness rests on a NEGATIVE claim, which is why I re-ran the full search rather than checking internal consistency. A coordinator should note that the record is only as durable as the corpus it searched: if a future artifact enumerates supported filesystems, this record becomes stale and the laterAct's other limb reopens.

The tcbV45 citation hedges its Codex standing rather than asserting one for this cycle ('Codex independently reviewed on a prior TCB cycle; this act does not invent a Codex verdict for this subject'). That is the correct handling under a usage-limited Codex and is worth noting as good practice.
